references.text: Moses warns against worshipping the sun, moon, and stars—the host of heaven—which the Lord has allotted to all peoples under the heavens.
The warning against following other gods that the people have not known, parallel with the prohibition against worshipping foreign gods.
Describes how the people turned away and worshipped other gods, serving deities they did not know.
King Josiah removed the idolatrous priests whom the kings of Judah had appointed to burn incense for Baal, the sun, the moon, the constellations, and all the host of heaven.
The prophet Jeremiah describes how the people loved, served, and followed the sun, the moon, and all the host of heaven.
Ezekiel sees in a vision that men worship the sun at the entrance to the Lord's temple, with their backs turned toward the temple.
Zephaniah prophesies judgment against those who worship the host of heaven on the rooftops and against those who worship and swear by the Lord but also by Milcom.
Stephen quotes the prophets and describes how God turned away and let them worship the host of heaven.
